speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. Since you are a newborn, I will rely on your parents to describe any symptoms you are experiencing. To begin, how old is your baby in days, and have they developed a fever or seemed unusually lethargic?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing that background; given the lack of prenatal care and unknown immunization status, I need to know if the newborn has been feeding well, gaining weight, or if there are any signs of jaundice or respiratory distress?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome

The combination of a continuous heart murmur (likely a patent ductus arteriosus), bluish macules (blueberry muffin rash), and cataracts is highly specific for this syndrome. I will request a Rubella IgM test and echocardiogram to confirm.
